def-anyonic-fusion-path-space:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$, so it is finite semisimple, rigid, monoidal, and has simple unit [[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects and let $n\ge0$. Set $T_0=b$ and recursively fix the left-associated parenthesization $T_{j+1}:=T_j\otimes a$. The **fixed-boundary anyonic path space** is

$$H_{a,n;b,c}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n).$$

For simple labels $x,y$, define the split multiplicity space $W_{x,a}^y:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(y,x\otimes a)$. A fusion path is a sequence of simple labels $x_0=b,x_1,\ldots,x_n=c$ together with, for every $1\le j\le n$, one basis index $\mu_j$ in a chosen basis $B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ of $W_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$. The basis index is retained even when distinct indices have the same adjacent labels. Fusion rules are the nonnegative integers $N_{x a}^{y}$ in $[x][a]=\sum_yN_{x a}^{y}[y]$ [[def-fusion-rules]].

If $i_j\in B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ is the selected inclusion $x_j\to x_{j-1}\otimes a$, define the path composite by $\gamma_0:=\operatorname{id}_b$ and $\gamma_j:=(\gamma_{j-1}\otimes\operatorname{id}_a)\circ i_j:x_j\to T_j$. For $x_n=c$, $\gamma_n$ is a vector in $H_{a,n;b,c}$. The next lemma proves these composites form a basis and computes the dimension. No Hilbert-space or physical Hamiltonian structure is part of this definition.
def-categorical-object-and-operator-inve:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category with unit $\mathbf1$. Its Grothendieck fusion ring $K_0(\mathcal C)$ is the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with multiplication induced by tensor product and coefficients given by the fusion rules of [[def-fusion-rules]].

- An object $X$ is **tensor-invertible** if there is an object $Y$ with $X\otimes Y\cong\mathbf1$ and $Y\otimes X\cong\mathbf1$.
- A class $[X]$ is a **fusion-ring unit** if it has a two-sided multiplicative inverse in $K_0(\mathcal C)$; that inverse may have negative integer coefficients in the simple-object basis.
- A linear operator is **invertible** only relative to a specified vector space $H$ and operator $T:H\to H$: it must have a two-sided inverse $S:H\to H$ with $ST=TS=I_H$.

These definitions concern different objects: categorical tensor product, a ring with virtual classes, and a chosen representation on a vector space.
lem-anyonic-fusion-path-basis:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex fusion category, let $a,b,c$ be simple objects, and fix a basis $B_{x,a}^y$ of every finite-dimensional split space $W_{x,a}^y=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(y,x\otimes a)$. For every admissible path $x_0=b,\ldots,x_n=c$ and every tuple of vertex indices $\mu_j\in B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$, the composite maps of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]] form a basis of $H_{a,n;b,c}$. Consequently,

$$\dim H_{a,n;b,c}=\sum_{\substack{x_0=b,\ x_n=c\\x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}\text{ simple}}}\prod_{j=1}^n N_{x_{j-1}a}^{x_j}.$$

The empty product is $1$ when $b\cong c$ and $0$ otherwise.
thm-anyonic-path-space-is-hilbert-under-:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary fusion category, and use orthonormal bases in each split space $W_{x,a}^y=\operatorname{Hom}(y,x\otimes a)$, equivalently the adjoints of orthonormal bases of $V_{x a}^y=\operatorname{Hom}(x\otimes a,y)$. Give $H_{a,n;b,c}=\operatorname{Hom}(c,T_n)$ the Hom-space inner product linear in the first variable, determined by $g^\dagger f=\langle f,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$. Then the path composites of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]] are an orthonormal basis of $H_{a,n;b,c}$.
def-anyonic-frobenius-schur-sign:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$, with pivotal structure and spherical dimension as in [[def-pivotal-structure]], [[def-spherical-structure]], and [[def-the-dimension-of-an-object-relative-to-a-pivotal-structure]]. Let $a$ be a self-dual simple object with $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$. Choose a unit vector $v:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ spanning the one-dimensional vacuum split space and let $d_a>0$ be its positive spherical dimension.

A **normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum** is a supplied pair of maps $\operatorname{coev}:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ and $\operatorname{ev}:a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$ of the form

$$\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt{d_a}\,v,\qquad \operatorname{ev}=\kappa_a\sqrt{d_a}\,v^\dagger,$$

where $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the two duality zig-zag identities hold after the self-duality identification, using the left-dual convention of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]. We call $\kappa_a$ the **Frobenius–Schur sign in this normalized cup/cap convention**. It is not a braiding or $R$-symbol phase.

This item records supplied normalized duality data; it does not assert that every self-dual simple object admits the displayed gauge or prove a trace, ribbon, or category-equivalence theorem. An example must supply the datum or compute the sign from coherent normalized F-data; fusion rules alone do not specify it.
def-anyonic-local-channel-projector:
## Definition

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $F_i$ be the typed sequence of associator changes carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree; each local matrix is the F-symbol of [[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]], with rows and columns as in that Definition. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction.

The coordinate convention is illustrated below: vectors move from the fixed tree to the pair-first tree by $F_i$, the channel projection acts there, and $F_i^{-1}$ returns to the fixed tree. The curved arrow denotes the defined composite, not an additional morphism.

```tikzcd
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{fixed}} \arrow[r,"F_i"] \arrow[rrr,bend right=35,"P_{i,s}"'] & \mathcal H_{\mathrm{pair}} \arrow[r,"\Pi_s"] & \mathcal H_{\mathrm{pair}} \arrow[r,"F_i^{-1}"] & \mathcal H_{\mathrm{fixed}}
```
lem-anyonic-vacuum-f-symbol-frobenius-sc:
## Statement

Let $a$ and $(v,\operatorname{ev},\operatorname{coev},d_a,\kappa_a)$ be as in [[def-anyonic-frobenius-schur-sign]]. In the multiplicity-free vacuum-normalized gauge of [[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]],

$$\left(F^{aaa}_a\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}=\frac{\kappa_a}{d_a},\qquad \delta_a:=\frac{1}{\left((F^{aaa}_a)^{-1}\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}}=\kappa_a d_a.$$
prop-fibonacci-fusion-ring-unit-is-not-t:
## Statement

In the coherent Fibonacci category [[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-data]], with simple objects $\mathbf1,\tau$ and $\tau\otimes\tau\cong\mathbf1\oplus\tau$, the fusion-ring class $[\tau]$ is a unit but the object $\tau$ is not tensor-invertible in the sense of [[def-categorical-object-and-operator-invertibility]].
thm-anyonic-channel-projectors-are-repar:
## Statement

For fixed ordered tensor inputs and fixed source and target parenthesizations, any two sequences of canonical associator F-moves between them induce the same coordinate map. Consequently, conjugating a fixed pair-channel projection by either sequence gives the same operator on the fusion-path space.
thm-anyonic-local-channel-projectors-are:
## Statement

For a unitary fusion category and any fixed adjacent pair of simple site charges, the family $(P_{i,s})_s$ from [[def-anyonic-local-channel-projector]] is pairwise orthogonal, self-adjoint, and idempotent, and its sum over all simple pair outputs $s$ is the identity on the path space.
lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon:
## Statement

Put $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{0,1\}$, with $0=\mathbf1$, $1=\eta$, and a third simple $D$. Use $ab=a+b$, $aD=Da=D$, and $DD=0\oplus1$, with summands ordered $(0,1)$ and every nonzero elementary fusion multiplicity equal to one. Let $d=\sqrt2$, $\kappa\in\{-1,1\}$, $\tau=\kappa/d$, $\chi(a,b)=(-1)^{ab}$, $u(0)=1$, $u(1)=i$, and choose $\beta$ of modulus one with $\beta^2=\tau(1+i)$. There is a unitary skeletal spherical ribbon fusion category with canonical orthonormal summand vertices and the following complete normal data. All admissible one-dimensional F blocks are $1$, except $F_D^{\eta D\eta}=F_\eta^{D\eta D}=-1$, and
$$F_D^{DDD}=\frac\kappa{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Rows are right-tree channels $(f,1,1)$ and columns left-tree channels $(e,1,1)$ in the inverse-precomposition convention. Unit blocks are identities and impossible channels have the unique empty matrix. The associator permutes the $DD$ summand by addition of a group input when needed; its complete formula and pentagon are proved below.

The object braiding is $c_{a,b}=\chi(a,b)$, $c_{a,D}=c_{D,a}=u(a)$, and $c_{D,D}^g=\beta/u(g)$. The pullback R symbols are their inverses, in the specified canonical vertices. Both hexagons hold in every channel. The normalized self-duality has $\operatorname{coev}_D=\sqrt d\,i_{DD}^0$, $\operatorname{ev}_D=\kappa\sqrt d\,p_{DD}^0$, FS sign $\kappa$, positive pivotal dimension $d$, and twist $\theta_D=\kappa/\beta$; $\eta$ has dimension and FS sign one and twist $-1$. The canonical left-dual tensorator is $\kappa$ on both $DD$ channels and one on all other channels; its double-dual tensorator is one on all ten admissible channels. Relative to those duals $j_D=\kappa$, $j_0=j_\eta=1$, and $j_{a\otimes b}=\nu_{a,b}(j_a\otimes j_b)$ holds channel by channel. For explicit phase specializations write $s=e^{\pi i/8}$. These assertions construct the full category; they do not assume a sector example as a supplier.
lem-ell-four-root-ising-gauge-and-chiral:
## Statement

Set $q=e^{\pi i/4}$, $s=e^{\pi i/8}$ and $d=\sqrt2$. The specified rank-one tilting negligible quotient is ribbon-equivalent to the normal-data category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]] at $\kappa=-1$, $\beta_-=-s^{-3}$, with labels $p_0=\mathbf1$, $p_1=D$, $p_2=\eta$. The full explicit normalized trivalent gauge is given in the proof using its negative-loop cup $w$, cap $b$, and $p_2=1+wb/d$. It gives $F_D^{DDD}=-2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, FS sign $-1$, positive dimension $\sqrt2$, and $\theta_D=s^3$.

Multiplying the associator by $\omega(x,y,z)=(-1)^{|x||y||z|}$ and the braiding by $(-i)^{|x||y|}$, with $D$ odd and group objects even, gives the distinct $\kappa=+1$, $\beta_+=s$ category. Flip the $D$ evaluation and keep its coevaluation. Its complete pullback R data are $R_{DD}^0=s^{-1}$, $R_{DD}^\eta=i s^{-1}$, $R_{\eta D}^D=R_{D\eta}^D=-i$, $R_{\eta\eta}^0=-1$, and unit entries one. Its twist is $\theta_D=s^{-1}$ in the actual pullback orientation. This is an associator/braiding conversion, not a vertex gauge equivalence or an unmodified positive-loop pivotal TL equivalence. Reversing its braiding and twist is a further explicitly different chirality operation.
thm-ising-periodic-two-sector-and-line-r:
## Statement

Use either coherent $\kappa$ category of [[lem-ising-unitary-normal-data-and-ribbon-coherence]], with reference charge $D$. For $L\ge1$, a periodic path $(x_1,\ldots,x_L)$ obeys $x_iD\supset x_{i+1}$ and $x_{L+1}=x_1$, with every elementary fusion index retained. Odd $L$ gives zero space. For $L=2N$, $N\ge1$, the complete orthonormal path space is $H\oplus\bar H$, each sector of dimension $2^N$, with the explicit bit identifications in the proof. These identifications intertwine every vacuum pair projector, including wraparound:
$$P_{2j-1}|_H=(1+X_j)/2,\quad P_{2j}|_H=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,$$
$$P_{2j-1}|_{\bar H}=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,\quad P_{2j}|_{\bar H}=(1+X_{j+1})/2.$$
All bit indices are modulo $N$. For $N=1$ the bond is the identity; no three-distinct-site cyclic TL assertion is made for this length-two identification.

Let $C|b_1\cdots b_N\rangle=|b_2\cdots b_Nb_1\rangle$, $Q=\prod_jX_j$, and
$$K_{c,b}=2^{-N/2}(-1)^{\sum_jc_j(b_{j-1}+b_j)}.$$
The one-step periodic path shift and the annular line maps defined by the full cyclic F contraction satisfy
$$T=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\I&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y_\eta=\operatorname{diag}(Q,Q),\quad Y_D=\kappa^N\begin{pmatrix}0&K^\dagger\\K&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
They obey $TP_iT^{-1}=P_{i-1}$, $Y_D^2=I+Y_\eta$, $Y_\eta^2=I$, $Y_\eta Y_D=Y_DY_\eta=Y_D$, and each line map commutes with every represented $P_i$ and with $T$. In contrast the specified normalized single-chain map obeys $(K/\sqrt2)^2=(I+Q)C^{-1}/2$. The proof supplies all wrapping, kernel, rank, Hamiltonian, and intertwining assertions on the full two-sector space, without a total-flux or global-spin-parity projection.
